explainer.title: MeshCore Ultrasonic Sensor — Sender + Receiver
explainer.body:
This kit is a pair of MeshCore devices that bridge a MaxBotix ultrasonic distance sensor to the internet over LoRa.

  • Sender — a Rook (nRF52840) that reads the ultrasonic sensor and transmits [SENSOR] dist=... batt=... LoRa DMs.
  • Receiver — a Heltec V3 (ESP32-S3) that receives, ACKs, and POSTs the reading to Bayou over WiFi.

Setup is three steps: flash the firmware onto both devices, get them to exchange identities so they can talk to each other, then configure WiFi and any other settings from the serial console.

flashingSection.title: Flashing the Firmware
flashingSection.intro: Both devices need firmware installed once. Pick a device below to flash it. The receiver flashes directly from your browser using Web Serial. The sender flashes by dragging its .uf2 file onto a USB drive that appears when you double-tap the reset button (Adafruit nRF52 UF2 bootloader — no external tool needed).

contactExchange.title: Connecting Sender and Receiver via Advert
contactExchange.content:
Before the sender can transmit readings to the receiver, both devices need to know each other's identity (public keys). The easiest way is to power both devices up next to each other and trigger each one to broadcast an advert — a small LoRa packet containing its identity and name — using its on-board button. The other device hears the advert and auto-adds it as a contact.

  1. Power up both devices next to each other. A few meters apart is plenty for indoor testing.
  2. On the receiver: short-press the user button repeatedly to cycle the OLED through pages, and stop when you see the Advert page.
  3. Long-press the button. The screen shows "Advert sent!" — the receiver has broadcast its identity, and the sender will hear it and add the receiver to its contacts.
  4. Now repeat on the sender: short-press to cycle to the Advert page, then long-press to send. The receiver hears and adds the sender.

Both devices now know each other. You can verify by opening either device's serial console (see next section) and running list — the other device should appear in the contacts list.

configuration.title: Configuring Other Settings (WiFi, Measurement Interval, etc.)
configuration.intro:
What is the serial console?

The serial console is a text interface to the device, exposed over USB. This page opens a serial connection directly in your browser — no external tool needed. It uses the Web Serial API, which works in Chrome and Edge on desktop (not Firefox or Safari, and not on mobile).

How to connect
  1. Plug the device into your computer via USB.
  2. Click Open Serial Console above.
  3. A browser dialog appears listing serial ports — pick the one for your device. The Rook usually shows up as USB Serial (Nordic UART), the Heltec as CP210x (Silicon Labs bridge).
  4. Type help and press Enter — the device lists every command it understands. Reference copies of that help output for each device are shown below so you know what to expect.
configuration.commonSettings:
Common settings
  • Setting the sender's target — sender only: after the sender and receiver know each other (see section 3), tell the sender which contact to transmit to. On the sender's console:
    list
target Receiver
    list shows every known contact — the receiver appears with its name (default Receiver). target Receiver locks the send target so every sensor reading goes to that contact.
  • WiFi credentials — receiver only:
    set wifi_ssid your-network-name
set wifi_password your-network-password
reboot
  • Measurement interval — sender only: set interval 60 sends every 60 seconds (minimum 10).
  • Node name — either device: set name My-Sensor changes the name shown in adverts and on the OLED.
  • Bayou keys — receiver only: baked into the firmware by default. Override with set bayou_public_key ... and set bayou_private_key ... to point at a different Bayou instance.

helpText.sender:
Commands:
   card                  - show your biz card for sharing
   import <biz card>     - import a contact's biz card
   list {n}              - list contacts (last n)
   purge                 - clear all contacts
   target                - show current targets
   target add <name>     - add a send target (max 4)
   target remove <name>  - remove a send target
   target clear          - clear all targets
   target <name>         - set to single target (replaces all)
   to <name>             - alias for 'target <name>'
   send                  - send a reading now
   set name <name>       - set node name
   set node_id <id>      - set node ID (1-65535)
   set interval <secs>   - set send interval (min 10)
   advert                - send advertisement
   ver                   - show firmware version
   help                  - show this help
helpText.receiver:
Commands:
   card                          - show biz card
   import <biz card>             - import a contact
   list {n}                      - list contacts (* = favourite)
   purge                         - clear all contacts
   favourite <name>              - protect contact from eviction
   unfavourite <name>            - clear favourite flag
   advert                        - send advertisement
   status                        - show WiFi/Bayou/last data
   show_settings                 - show node config + favourites
   set name <name>               - set node name
   set wifi_ssid <ssid>          - set WiFi SSID (reboot)
   set wifi_password <pwd>       - set WiFi password (reboot)
   set bayou_public_key <key>    - set Bayou public key
   set bayou_private_key <key>   - set Bayou private key
   ver                           - firmware version
   help                          - show this help

notice.uf2Manual:
How to flash this Rook
1. Double-tap the reset button — a NICENANO USB drive appears.
2. Click Download below and drag the .uf2 file onto that drive.
3. The device reboots automatically when the copy finishes.

commands.set wifi_ssid: Set WiFi SSID {ssid} (receiver, reboot to apply)
commands.set wifi_password: Set WiFi password {pw} (receiver, reboot to apply)

v3-ultrasonic.notes:
v3-ultrasonic build
* MaxBotix MB7388 on Serial1 (D0 = P0.08, "RX1")
* Transmits [SENSOR] dist=... batt=... to the paired receiver
* Pair by running `advert` on the receiver, then `target <receiver-name>` on the sender

files.name: heltec_v3_receiver_ultrasonic_v3.bin
files.title: heltec_v3_receiver_ultrasonic_v3.bin — app only (safe update, keeps bootloader)

v3-ultrasonic.notes:
v3-ultrasonic build
* Receives LoRa DMs, posts to Bayou
* Bayou defaults baked in (bayou_public_key = mfupcqtx34ee, bayou_private_key = t3w7v5zpk8ya) — override with `set bayou_public_key ...` / `set bayou_private_key ...`
* Set WiFi with `set wifi_ssid ...` and `set wifi_password ...`, then `reboot`
